question: Why does one cigarette after months without smoking so often turn into a full relapse?
answer: Because of how the slip is read. Marlatt called it the abstinence violation effect: a person who takes a lapse as proof of having no willpower feels the whole effort is ruined, and gives up. Read as a mistake in one situation, to be planned for next time, the same cigarette stays a single lapse.
move: Treat a slip as one event to learn from, not a verdict.
ask: Which habit did I drop after one bad day, and could I simply start again tomorrow?
reference: Marlatt and Gordon (eds.), Relapse Prevention: Maintenance Strategies in the Treatment of Addictive Behaviors, Guilford Press, 1985
